Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-08 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Recording id: ff-20251008-9c1d
Attendees: Alex (AE, Redwood); Priya (SE, Redwood); Tom (CTO, Northview); Sara (Platform Eng); Ellen (Head Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be partial): Discussed integration options and network/VPC constraints, agreed to run a perf POC and exchange security docs.

[00:00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick roll call?
[00:00:06] Tom: Tom here.
[00:00:08] Sara: Sara, hi.
[00:00:09] Ellen: Ellen.
[00:00:12] Alex: Alex, and Priya's on the line too. We'll keep this to an hour, we want to understand your integration surface — SDKs, how you're thinking about the gateway/proxy, quotas, and observability.
[00:00:32] Priya: Hi team, quick note — I'll mostly focus on the technical integration patterns, happy to pair on a sample gateway.
[00:00:42] Tom: Great. High level, Northview runs a mix of customer-facing apps and internal triage workflows. We're evaluating Redwood because we need predictable latency and strict data residency for PHI.
[00:00:58] Ellen: And controls — SSO, audit logs, KMS integration are must-haves. SOC2 is a baseline.
[00:01:10] Alex: Understood. Priya, do you want to sketch out the SDK and gateway options?
[00:01:17] Priya: Sure. There are three common patterns we see: direct SDK calls from app servers into Redwood hosted endpoints, a gateway/proxy layer that centralizes auth, quotas, and caching, or a private deployment where the control plane is separate and model inference runs in customer VPC/on-prem.
[00:01:45] Priya: For SDKs we have Python and Node clients — they support streaming, function/tool calling, structured outputs, and are compatible with LangChain and LlamaIndex wrappers. Example: with LangChain you can use our LLM wrapper, and the same for embeddings.
[00:02:05] Sara: Our stack is FastAPI behind an nginx ingress on k8s. Ideally we'd have a lightweight gateway sidecar or central proxy that enforces per-tenant rate limits and token quotas before requests hit Redwood.
[00:02:20] Priya: That's a common design. Redwood's token accounting is precise (per-request token counts), so the gateway can decrement quotas; we also expose an API for current usage and quota checks. We can share a snippet for a FastAPI middleware.
[00:02:41] Tom: What's the latency cost of doing that extra hop? We're trying to keep tail latency sub-150ms for short prompts.
[00:02:50] Priya: If the gateway is just auth and accounting, overhead is small — typically 5–15ms for a well-placed sidecar. Bigger costs come from network egress to Hosted or from added batching windows when you try to batch requests. With Dedicated you get lower jitter because of reserved GPU pools.
[00:03:12] Alex: On batching — Priya, can you explain continuous batching and KV cache tradeoffs?
[00:03:18] Priya: Sure. Redwood supports workload-aware continuous batching: requests are grouped by model/seq-length and dispatched. For retrieval-heavy flows we recommend KV/prefix caching — that saves both latency and tokens by reusing prefix computations. But caching complexity increases with multi-tenant data isolation.
[00:03:38] Sara: For PHI we want strict tenancy; KV cache needs to be per-tenant or encrypted. Is that doable?
[00:03:45] Priya: Yes, per-tenant caches are supported on Dedicated/Private. On Hosted we can do namespaced caches with encryption, but you'd likely want Private for strict air-gapped requirements.
[00:03:59] Ellen: Also want to confirm KMS integration — we use AWS KMS and HSM for key storage.
[00:04:06] Alex: Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM integration and can route keys through your KMS. We'll attach the whitepaper in the follow-up.
[00:04:16] Tom: How about SDK auth — SSO or service accounts? We need RBAC for teams, scoped tokens.
[00:04:25] Alex: We support short-lived service tokens for apps, plus SSO + SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC is available in the Console, and you can bind routes to roles.
[00:04:35] [00:04:40] Speaker 3: (inaudible)
[00:04:45] Priya: Observability — we expose traces, metrics, and logs. You can stream traces via OpenTelemetry, push metrics to Datadog/Prometheus, and get token-level cost breakdowns in the Console. For the gateway we recommend propagating trace headers so Redwood can join traces.
[00:05:05] Sara: We use Datadog and have an OpenTelemetry collector. Can we get example spans?
[00:05:11] Priya: Yes, we'll share OTel example config and sample spans. The spans include model name, latency breakdown (decode, kernel, queue), token counts, and user-id/tenant-id fields. Note: redact PHI fields before exporting.
[00:05:30] Tom: LangChain integrations — any gotchas? We currently use LangChain agents in a few services and a LlamaIndex-based search layer for notes.
[00:05:40] Priya: Workflows are straightforward. Two things to watch: (1) streaming vs non-streaming outputs — agents often rely on streaming; make sure you enable streaming in the SDK and route stream responses through your gateway, and (2) function-calls — LangChain/agents may do structured function calling; the SDK supports that. For LlamaIndex, the embeddings pipeline and chunking settings need to match Redwood's tokenization assumptions to avoid over-chunking and cost surprises.
[00:06:12] Sara: On quotas — we want both rate limits (req/s) per tenant and monthly token caps. Can the gateway enforce both?
[00:06:21] Priya: Yes. Typical pattern: gateway enforces soft rate limits with leaky-bucket token buckets, and consults Redwood's usage API for token balances. You can also get webhook alerts when quotas near limits. On Dedicated we can do enforced hard caps at the infra layer.
[00:06:40] Tom: For our throughput goals: initial pilot 200 req/s with spikes to 500 req/s for certain workflows. What's the rough footprint?
[00:06:50] Priya: Depends on model and prompt length. For a 2–4k token model, 200–500 req/s typically needs Dedicated reservations with autoscaling policies. We'll propose a POC config: 2 dedicated pools — one for low-latency short prompts and one for long-context retrieval-heavy jobs.
[00:07:12] Ellen: Compliance question — audit logs need to show who invoked what model and when, with request/response hashes retained for X days. Can Redwood provide immutable audit trails?
[00:07:23] Alex: Yes, audit logs with immutable storage and configurable retention are available; for Private you can ship logs to your SIEM. We'll include the retention and export options in the security pack.
[00:07:35] Tom: Pricing — we need a TCO comparison. We do a lot of embeddings for search; embedding unit costs are significant.
[00:07:43] Alex: We'll produce a TCO worksheet — cost per embedding call, per-token gen costs, plus infra and reserved slot amortization for Dedicated. Also show the math for caching and batching savings.
[00:07:57] [00:08:03] Speaker 2: (crosstalk)
[00:08:10] Priya: A quick note on gateway proxies: if you centralize state in the proxy (like a user session cache) you get simpler enforcement, but single-hop failure modes increase. We usually recommend a stateless or sharded proxy with Redis for quota counters.
[00:08:30] Sara: We already have Redis clusters per region. Good.
[00:08:35] Tom: Is there any managed proxy option from Redwood?
[00:08:40] Alex: We don't host customer-side proxies, but Redwood's SDKs have middleware and we provide a reference gateway repo that you can run in k8s. For large customers we sometimes collaborate on a hardened gateway image.
[00:08:56] Priya: Also, if you're using Private, the control plane can still be Redwood-managed while inference runs in your VPC — that gives you the best of both for upgrades and model ops.
[00:09:12] Ellen: For the perf POC, will Redwood need our data? We prefer synthetic data first.
[00:09:20] Priya: Synthetic is fine for initial throughput/latency tests. For quality/regression, we'll want sample prompts but never store PHI in Redwood-hosted environments unless under appropriate agreements.
[00:09:33] Tom: Can we capture token-level traces and export them to our Datadog?
[00:09:38] Priya: Yes — either via OTel spans or by exporting detailed metrics. We'll send the sample ones.
[00:09:45] Sara: A small nit — our engineering org expects OpenAPI-first SDK snippets. Do you have auto-generated OpenAPI for the SDK?
[00:09:53] Alex: We provide API specs and OpenAPI JSON for our REST endpoints; the SDKs are thin wrappers. We'll attach the swagger/openapi artifact.
[00:10:02] Tom: Any latency SLOs for hosted?
[00:10:06] Alex: Hosted is best-effort with published P50/P95 profiles in the model catalog; Dedicated has SLA-backed latency targets and lower variability. We'll include sample latency graphs.
[00:10:18] [00:10:25] Priya: One gotcha — if you centralize embeddings requests through a single proxy and also do synchronous calls, you can get head-of-line blocking when a long retrieval job monopolizes the slot. We recommend separate routes for embeddings vs generative flows.
[00:10:43] Sara: Makes sense. We'll likely separate the pipelines.
[00:10:48] Tom: What about rate-limit headers? Can the SDK surface remaining tokens/quotas in responses?
[00:10:55] Priya: Yes, we return quota headers and a usage endpoint. You can show token budgets in your app dashboard.
[00:11:03] Ellen: Security — does Redwood support customer-managed network egress controls for Hosted? We need to ensure traffic to models doesn't traverse public internet in some cases.
[00:11:13] Alex: For Hosted, egress is over public endpoints; however we offer VPC peering and private-links on Dedicated and Private, which gives you control. We'll include network diagrams.
[00:11:27] [00:11:40] Speaker 1: (laughs)
[00:11:45] Priya: Operationally, observability hooks we recommend: propagate OTel trace id, emit model-level metrics (latency decode/kernel/queue), and log request metadata without PHI. Redwood Console surfaces cost and token breakout per route.
[00:12:05] Tom: Regarding LangChain — if we keep agents inside the gateway, do you see any security/model leakage concerns?
[00:12:13] Priya: If agents have external tool access, treat that as a separate attack surface. We recommend strict ACLs and per-agent identities, plus sanitized inputs/outputs in logs.
[00:12:27] Sara: On rollout strategy — we'd want to canary new models and have automatic fallback to smaller models under load. Is that supported?
[00:12:36] Alex: Yes, Redwood supports rollout policies: canary percentages, A/B, and automatic fallback to cheaper model variants if latency or error rates spike.
[00:12:46] Tom: Great. For the POC data flow — we'll send a sample flow: front-end -> FastAPI gateway -> Redwood (via sidecar) -> LlamaIndex re-ranker -> reply. Would that work?
[00:13:00] Priya: Yes, that's a typical flow. We'll test continuity with streaming and function calls in the POC.
[00:13:07] Ellen: Any contractual items we should know before a Private deployment? Support SLAs, on-prem install windows, and monthly minimums?
[00:13:16] Alex: We'll include a Private deployment checklist and a draft for enterprise terms. Private typically has a platform license plus services for deployment and a support tier.
[00:13:29] [00:13:40] Priya: Quick technical question from us: do you have hard per-tenant data retention policies today?
[00:13:46] Tom: We retain logs for 90 days and PII is tokenized. For PHI we need selective retention and deletion APIs.
[00:13:56] Priya: Redwood has deletion APIs and retention controls; for Private we can honor arbitrary retention windows and provide deletion proof.
[00:14:07] Tom: Anything else on observability?
[00:14:10] Sara: We want sampled request/response payloads stored for debugging; can we get redaction tooling?
[00:14:16] Priya: Yes, Redwood can do on-ingest redaction rules; otherwise ship to your SIEM after redaction.
[00:14:24] Ellen: Ok good.
[00:14:27] Alex: To recap — we'll send pricing/TCO, security docs, SDK/OpenAPI, FastAPI middleware example, OTel spans, and propose a perf POC. Does that match what you expect?
[00:14:42] Tom: Yes. Can we aim to have the POC next week?
[00:14:45] Alex: We'll try. Priya, availability?
[00:14:48] Priya: I can do Wednesday or Thursday.
[00:14:50] Sara: Thursday works for us.
[00:14:52] Alex: Great. We'll send calendar invite and pre-POC checklist.
